guidance.statement: Gross margin to be upward of 71% for FY27, taking into account higher commodity and dollar costs
EBITDA margin guidance of 25.5% to 26.5% for FY27, unchanged
R&D spend guided at 2.8% to 3% of sales for FY27
Capex guided at 6% to 7% of revenue for FY27
BSV growth guided at high teens (high double-digit) for FY27, with domestic around 17% and international around 25%
Consumer Healthcare expected to grow high single-digit to double-digit from Q2FY27 onwards
Chronic share targeted to rise from about 40% to 50% over the next 4 to 5 years
Acquisition-related debt to be fully repaid by FY28

operating_notes.text: CARE Ratings assigned CARE AA+ (Stable) long-term and CARE A1+ short-term ratings to ₹1,000 Cr of Mankind Pharma's bank facilities on 22 April 2026.
ICRA reaffirmed [ICRA]AA+ (Stable)/[ICRA]A1+ on ₹1,250 Cr fund-based limits and [ICRA]AA+ (Stable) on ₹5,000 Cr NCDs, and assigned [ICRA]A1+ to ₹600 Cr commercial paper.
Mankind decided to avail the lower tax rate regime (25.17%) from FY 2026-27.
The company recognized an impairment loss of ₹13.44 Cr on a suspended greenfield project in Hyderabad.
Executive directors waived FY26 commissions to strengthen the company's cash position for expansion.
Q4FY26 domestic secondary sales grew 8.7% against IPM growth of 10.7%; cardiac grew 14.7% and anti-diabetes 11.6%.
Exports revenue was ₹2,061 Cr in FY26 versus ₹1,532 Cr in FY25; Mankind (ex-BSV) has 48 products launched in the US.
Consumer healthcare modern trade and e-commerce share rose to 13% in FY26 from 9% in FY25.
Q4FY26 secondary sales grew 8.7% vs IPM growth of 10.7%; cardiac grew 14.7% and anti-diabetes 11.6%, with chronic share up 120 bps YoY to ~40%.
FY26 exports ₹2,061 Cr (+34.5% YoY) but Q4FY26 exports grew only 4.2% on geopolitical headwinds; Mankind ex-BSV has 48 products launched in the US.
Consumer healthcare MT & e-commerce share rose to 13% in FY26 from 9% in FY25, supported by 57% growth.
Chronic therapy contribution reached ~40% of sales in Q4FY26.
Mankind Lifesciences acquired remaining 10% stake in Upakarma Ayurveda for ₹0.75 Cr, making it a 100% WOS.
IQVIA secondary sales grew 12.7% in Q1FY27 with volume growth of 4.7%, up 220 bps YoY, and Mankind holds 15.2% prescription share, ranked first.
New-product contribution was 2.8% versus IPM's 4.1% in Q1FY27, one reason overall growth trailed the market.
Anti-diabetes covered market rose from 56% in FY21 to 74% in FY26, with rank improving to 7 and market share of 4.5%.
ACTx is a Belgium-incorporated biotech with lead CAR-T programs in non-Hodgkin lymphoma and small cell lung cancer, R&D teams in US and EU, and nil turnover.

timeline.summary: 22 Apr 2026: CARE Ratings assigned CARE AA+ (Stable) / CARE A1+ to Mankind Pharma's ₹1,000 Cr long-term/short-term bank facilities.
12 May 2026: ICRA reaffirmed Mankind Pharma at [ICRA]AA+ (Stable)/[ICRA]A1+ on ₹1,250 Cr fund-based limits and ₹5,000 Cr NCDs, and assigned [ICRA]A1+ to ₹600 Cr of commercial paper.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹3,442.93 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹554.35 Cr.
Mankind Pharma completed the ₹13,768 Cr acquisition of Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV) and approved a ₹500 Cr investment in its Medicare subsidiary.
19 May 2026: Mankind Pharma's Q4/FY26 investor presentation showed Q4FY26 revenue of ₹3,443 Cr (+11.8% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 26.4%, with FY26 PAT down 3.4% to ₹1,938 Cr.

19 May 2026: Mankind Pharma's Q4FY26 press release showed revenue ₹3,443 Cr (+11.8% YoY), adjusted EBITDA margin 27.1% and PAT ₹559 Cr (+30.4%); FY26 revenue ₹14,278 Cr (+17.0%) with PAT down 3.4% to ₹1,938 Cr.
Mankind Pharma Limited shared the Q4 & FY26 Investor Conference Call recording on May 20, 2026, available at the company’s website.
26 May 2026: Mankind Pharma filed the transcript of its Q4 & FY26 earnings conference call held on May 20, 2026.
Mankind Lifesciences acquired the remaining 10% stake in Upakarma Ayurveda for ₹0.75 crore on June 2, 2026.
Q1FY27 (Jul 30, 2026 call): revenue rose 12.9% YoY to ₹4,031 Cr and EBITDA margin expanded 250 bps to 26.3%, with net debt cut to ₹3,377 Cr (0.9x adjusted EBITDA) after a ₹1,250 Cr NCD repayment.
2026-10-15: Board approved up to EUR 45 Mn additional investment in Mankind Pharma (Netherlands) B.V. to fund a EUR 48 Mn, 70% acquisition of Belgium CAR-T biotech Armed Cell Therapeutics.

watchlist.response: Rajeev Juneja called it a 'strategical approach' rather than caution, citing 20-plus competitors and 35-40 brands; Prakash Agarwal said a price war on a partnered product would not be profitable. No launch-volume or revenue target given.
watchlist.text: Kunal and Ritika pressed on why Mankind held back from the first wave of GLP-1/Semaglutide launches despite a prior tie-up

watchlist.response: CFO attributed the conservatism solely to the West Asia crisis and pointed to the unchanged EBITDA guidance of 25.5-26.5%.
